chunks: Sama‘ah narrated from Abī ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام that he said:
Indeed, when one of you falls ill, he calls the physician and gives him payment; and when he has a need with a ruler, he bribes the gatekeeper and gives him.

But if, when one of you is struck by a grave matter, he were to turn in alarm to Allah, the Exalted, purify himself, give charity—whether little or much—then enter the mosque and pray two rak‘ahs, then praise Allah and extol Him, and invoke blessings upon the Prophet and his Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام, then say: “O Allah, if You grant me well-being from my illness, or return me from my journey, or grant me well-being from what I fear of such-and-such,” Allah would surely grant him that.
And this is the binding oath, and that which Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has made incumbent upon him in gratitude.

key_terms.أَثْنَى عَلَيْهِ: He praised and extolled Allah before making the request.
key_terms.أَهْلِ بَيْتِهِ: The family of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم upon whom blessings are invoked.
key_terms.الشُّكْرِ: Gratitude shown to Allah after receiving relief or blessing.
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدَ: The mosque, where the person goes to perform the prayer of need.
key_terms.الْيَمِينُ الْوَاجِبَةُ: A binding oath or vow described as obligatory in this context of gratitude.
key_terms.بِصَدَقَةٍ: An act of charity given before making the supplication, whether small or large.
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْنِ: Two units of salat (prayer) performed in this devotional act.
key_terms.فَتَطَهَّرَ: He purified himself ritually before turning to worship and supplication.

ai.seo_question: What should a believer do in Shia hadith when facing hardship, illness, or fear?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that in times of distress, a believer should turn to Allah through taharah, charity, salat, praise, and du'a rather than relying only on worldly means. It emphasizes a devotional response to hardship and presents this vow of gratitude as something weighty and binding before Allah.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1544 - Sama’a narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) that He said:
"When one of you falls ill, he calls for the physician and pays him. When someone has a need from a ruler, he bribes the gatekeeper and gives him.

However, if one of you is struck by an overwhelming concern and turns to Allah (swt), the Exalted, purifies himself (performs ablution), gives charity (whether small or large), then enters the mosque, prays two units (rak'ahs) of prayer, praises and glorifies Allah (swt), and invokes blessings upon the Prophet and his family (as), then says: 'O’ Allah (swt), if You cure me of my illness, or return me safely from my journey, or protect me from what I fear of such and such (mentioning the specific concern),' Allah (swt) would grant him that.
This is the binding oath, and it is what Allah (swt), the Blessed and Exalted, has made incumbent upon one as an expression of gratitude."
